findings.note: The GREEN evidence was not captured against the artifact under review. TEST-019-static-q reports 'the Risk-Upgrade Gate section (line 31) precedes the specs/<feature>/ generation step (line 103)' in both twins at HEAD 4905c131; in the bundled staged SKILL.md the '## Risk-Upgrade Gate' heading is at file line 139 and the generation step at file line 211, i.e. ~108 lines were inserted ahead of the gate after the capture. The bundle header independently flags the implementation report's declared SHA-256 for this path as STALE. MANIFEST.sha256 is not in the bundle, so TEST-021b's assertion that the manifest digest matches the staged bytes cannot be confirmed for the current content either. For a Risk: high / Required Workflow: tdd task whose primary deliverable is this one hash-bound file, all 31 green assertions are therefore unverified against the bytes being reviewed and must be re-run and re-captured.

T-003's declared sole human-copy payload now carries another feature's content. The inserted block is epic-189-a1-project-context / ADR-0023 material (check-hook-activation-handshake, the G1-G4 CAPABILITY_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE gate table, the C1-C6 track-selection contract), none of which appears in this feature's requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md or acceptance-tests.md; the bundle's only other mentions of it are CHANGELOG entries for Issue #189. T-003's own implementation report lists this payload under 'Deliberately left alone' as 'unchanged from T-001's own resume'. Because this file is staged for application to the R-10 protected plugins/sdd-lite/skills/lite-spec/SKILL.md by T-001's runner, T-003's HUMAN APPLY STEP would install cross-feature content that T-003's suite never asserts and this task never reviewed. AC-021's 'touches only lite-spec/SKILL.md' is satisfied by path count but not by content ownership, and the new block sits ahead of the Risk-Upgrade Gate in the pre-Process control flow, an interaction with REQ-005's 'before beginning the Process' position that nothing in the bundle exercises.

Two checks marked required:true are recorded passes:false, so the default-FAIL verification contract does not pass and T-003 is not gate-ready by its own instrument. placeholder-scan is the harder of the two: verification/qg/shared/placeholder-scan.log ends 'Placeholder scan FAILED (5 finding(s)) ... exit: 1' against CHANGELOG.md, a file T-003 declares as one of its own Outputs, and the scanner's own message admits exactly two exits - implement properly, or explicit human acceptance in a quality-gate report. The contract comment concedes no quality-gate report exists for this feature (verification/qg/ holds logs only), so neither exit has been taken; the pre-existence proof at merge-base bd48ce8c is an argument for a human to accept, not an acceptance. regression is false on real, unwaived, non-designed-red failures (workflow-state, check-component-coverage, repository-release-validation) per the log's own 2026-08-25 verdict.

RED evidence does not cover most of the assertions it is cited as the pre-fix baseline for. T-003.red.log records 14 assertions (1 passed / 13 failed: 10 static, 3 functional, 1 defense-in-depth); the current suite records 31. No RED counterpart exists for static-g2, static-k through static-q, TEST-019-fixture-catalog, functional-registry-shape, functional-baseline, defense-in-depth-a/b/c, or TEST-021a/b/c - roughly 17 assertions, including every assertion added by the 2026-08-25 cross-model remediation. The red log is demonstrably from the pre-remediation suite: its static-g needle is the discredited 'regardless of whether the' fragment that the current suite replaced precisely because it discriminated nothing. The contract's justification for reuse ('independent of the later .PROPOSED-to-canonical path migration') covers the path change but not the added assertions, and Required Workflow is tdd on a Risk: high task.

The contract's spec_revision pin 2740928c9e9c45cd56644a0e22e4fb5fc3c270932eba9c8fecf4a8450780d437 is stale by the contract's own admission: it was computed 2026-08-19, before the 2026-08-21 AC-010 five-target amendment (9997091c) and its propagation commits, and the recomputed current value 466465e04248cb912635ed83435ff0c17e9805648e0caead7132ad6276a34d23 is recorded in the comment but deliberately not written into the field. The acceptance instrument for a Risk: high, Security-Sensitive task therefore certifies a specification revision that is not the one under review. Disclosure does not bind the pin; the re-issue is still owed.

The contract comment describes the evidence it names as 'freshly re-run this session: 14/14 both runtimes -- 10 static + 3 functional + 1 defense-in-depth', but the named log records 'Results: 31 passed, 0 failed' on both runtimes (19 static + fixture-catalog + 5 functional + 4 defense-in-depth + 3 TEST-021). The passes:true flag is correct, but the contract's own description of its evidence contradicts the evidence - the same contract-versus-log divergence class an earlier panel already caught on the regression and placeholder-scan flags.

The fixture declares upgrade_reasons ['financial_settlement'], a token absent from design.md's Data Plan catalog_version-2 vocabulary (the five seeded tokens plus public_package_registry, store_distribution, auto_update, code_signing, payments, multi_tenant, high_risk_migration). requirements.md Field Definitions states each fragment token 'is a lite_policy.upgrade_reasons value already validated against lite-upgrade-reason-catalog.json', so the fixture models a Registry state REQ-001's validator check (h) would reject fail-closed. The behaviour under test is unaffected (check-risk-upgrade deliberately does not re-validate catalog membership), but TEST-019-functional-c pins a token no conforming Capability could ever declare.

AC-021's 'no separate, REQ-005-specific application path introduced' is asserted only over the staging root's top level - find -maxdepth 1 in the sh twin, a non-recursive Get-ChildItem in the ps1 twin. A REQ-005-specific applier staged one directory down (for example human-copy/plugins/apply-lite-spec.ps1) would leave TEST-021c green, and the fixture's own forbidden_req005_application_paths list is never consulted by either twin.

Twin divergence in how the sole staged target and shared runner names are obtained: the ps1 twin reads them from the fixture catalog (ac_021.sole_staged_target / shared_application_runner) with a literal fallback, while the sh twin hard-codes both. The pair is presented as a runtime-equivalence check, but a corrupted or edited ac_021 block would move only the PowerShell half's expectations - the same twin-fidelity gap a prior round had to repair by hand in the Registry fixture.
